# LinkedIn DOM fixtures

Extraction is developed against these files, never against live LinkedIn.

That rule exists because it was broken twice. Both times the reader was fixed
against a fixture written from a guess, both times the guess was tidier than the
page LinkedIn actually ships, and both times the tests went green while the real
capture stayed broken. A live profile is the worst possible test surface: it
needs an authenticated session, it cannot be inspected from CI, and it changes
under you while you work.

## Two kinds of fixture

**`real-*.html` — recordings.** Produced by the extension's **Save DOM
snapshot** button. These are the authoritative evidence. Scrubbing happens
inside the page (`extension/snapshot.js`) so nothing unscrubbed ever leaves the
tab: every other person's name is replaced with a placeholder, the profile
owner is replaced consistently across title, URL slug and card, `<script>` and
`<code>` bodies are emptied (LinkedIn ships the entire profile as JSON in hidden
`<code>` elements — megabytes of personal data, none of it under test), signed
`licdn` query strings are dropped and long tokens masked. Hashed class names,
DOM order, nesting depth, `aria` attributes and the right-hand rail survive
untouched, because those are the test.

**`a`–`e` — reconstructions.** Generated by `generate-synthetic.mjs`. Written
from the `diagnoseVersion: 2` report of the page that actually broke, so the
work was not blocked on having a live profile to hand. Regenerate with:

```bash
node test/fixtures/linkedin/generate-synthetic.mjs
```

Prefer a recording over a reconstruction whenever one exists for the same shape.

## What each one is for

| File | Shape | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `a-authenticated-with-right-rail.html` | Signed-in profile, populated right rail | **The reference case.** Reproduces the reported bug exactly. |
| `b-no-right-rail.html` | Same profile, no rail | Proves the boundary fix does not depend on a rail being present. |
| `c-contact-info-overlay.html` | Contact-info modal, open | Email/phone/website live only here. Parsed by label, not position. |
| `d-accented-name-hungarian-location.html` | Accented name, Hungarian UI and location | Accent handling, and family-name-first ordering. |
| `e-mangled-two-identities.html` | A second `/in/` identity inside the top card | The boundary test must fail loudly and degrade to name-only. |

## The facts fixture (a) encodes

Taken from the real diagnostics, not invented:

- `totalH1: 0` — no `<h1>` anywhere. The name is anchor text.
- `#about` / `#experience` / `#education` / `#skills` all absent — no id anchors
  to locate sections by.
- Class names are hashed — nothing may be selected by class.
- The container the old reader mistook for the top card reported
  `liCount: 36, nested: 11` — it had swallowed the right-hand rail.
- `mailto: 0, tel: 0, outboundHosts: []` — contact details are **not** on the
  profile page.

Two details are reconstructions rather than observations, and are reasoned from
the two wrong values that were actually captured:

- **`"Keletso Thophego, CFP"` became the city** because the old `isPlace()` test
  was "contains a comma, no digits, under 100 characters" — which a credential
  suffix passes. The strings are kept verbatim in the fixture because the
  regression test asserts against them.
- **The rail precedes the profile's own text in source order.** A rail name
  could only win the headline if it came first in DOM order, which is how a
  CSS-positioned right column gets sourced.
